method.name: milp_transport
steps: Define parameters: supply[w], demand[p], cost_per_km[w,p], rate=30 EUR/km, distance[w,p] from table
Decision variables: x[w,p] >= 0 continuous (containers transported from warehouse w to port p)
Objective: minimize sum(w in W, p in P) x[w,p] * distance[w,p] * 30
Constraints: supply[w]: sum(p in P) x[w,p] = supply[w] for all w; demand[p]: sum(w in W) x[w,p] = demand[p] for all p
Solve with highs LP solver; variables naturally integer due to totally unimodular matrix

method.name: milp_transport_integer
steps: Define sets: warehouses W, ports P
Decision variables: x[w,p] >= 0 integer (container counts, must be whole units)
Same objective: minimize sum(w,p) x[w,p] * distance[w,p] * 30
Same supply and demand constraints as standard formulation
Solve with highs MILP solver; integer constraints ensure whole-container counts
Integer solution required because containers are discrete units

method.name: network_flow_transport
steps: Formulate as min-cost network flow: super-source connected to each warehouse with capacity=supply[w]; each port connected to super-sink with demand[p]; arcs between warehouses and ports with cost=distance*30
Decision variables: flow[f] >= 0 on each arc (continuous)
Flow conservation at intermediate nodes (warehouses and ports as transshipment nodes)
Solve as LP; due to network structure (supply/demand balanced, costs positive), solution is always integer
Use highs network simplex or standard LP solver
